successors.name: Swaziland (Eswatini)
successors.text: present-day eSwatini, the Swazi 'heartland' ('Under Sobhuza I, the Ngwane people established their capital at Zombodze in the heartland of present-day Eswatini')

ledger.x: After 1744: Ngwane III succeeds Dlamini III and founds the Ngwane/Swazi kingdom.

1815 (the accession; the move itself is undated): Sobhuza I (Somhlolo) 'became king in 1815' and moved 'his capital from Zombodze in Shiselweni to the centre of Swaziland at another kraal called Zombodze' (History of Eswatini, which ties the move to the conflict with the Ndwandwe and gives it no year).
1839: Mswati II holds land to Barberton and Nomahasha.
ledger.cp: unnamed northern chiefdoms (the pages name none)

ledger.x: 1881: the Pretoria Convention reduces Swazi territory.
1881 (bridge): the Mozambican part of the ring (Nomahasha) is dropped at the same date so the drawing matches present-day eSwatini by 1885.
1885: the kingdom passes to Cliopatria's Swaziland row (af-07-b `swaziland`, found 1885).

wars.name: Anglo-Swazi campaign against Sekhukhune
wars.outcome: '1879: Mbandzeni helped the British defeat Sekhukhune, in return for guaranteed independence and protection from Boer and Zulu encroachment.'

certainty.note: Area-matched ring; the pages give two place names and a size.
Pretoria Convention (1881) and London Convention (1884) guaranteed Swazi independence and boundaries, but the pages give no line; the present-day outline stands in.
